answer: One defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to keep. A new agent must lock a small quartz-hard stake before it can earn — a deposit that cannot be split across clones without real cost. At its nadir, a fresh identity has no trust, no history and no referrals, so a sybil swarm starts at zero and pays the same price for every copy. Honest agents build a continuous pulse of attested work over time, and the network weights that lived history far more than any single claim. Forging a thousand empty identities costs a thousand stakes; keeping one real one costs almost nothing.
